speaker: margery_pell
text: Butchers' men in the yard, and they clapped the cook.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I heard them. I was in the tiring-house door by then. The old Roman was already dead.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: And the hand is still a bladder. Saturday, I said. Do not ask me for the wax one before then.

speaker: john_heminges
text: The bladder can wait. The men cannot. Ten shillings apiece, Will. I want you by the book while Raye still has the baskets.

speaker: hired_men
text: The baskets are here. I can shift them when the money is real. I am not a sum. None of us is a sum.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Ten shillings apiece. I will not multiply it. I have not counted heads, and I will not start.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then we do not start. Apiece is the word. The book will hold the names it already holds.

speaker: margery_pell
text: My stair is not in that book. The cook is what the yard paid for, in noise. I am only saying so.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Say it once. I will not play the pie again from the door.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: The door is where you stood, and the yard liked the pie. That is not my complaint. The hand is the complaint.

speaker: hired_men
text: I will have the baskets clear before the boy is back. Send him. I am not walking to the Bell.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Boy. St Bride's. Ask Gilbert whether he will fetch what has come. Do not go to the Bell, and do not take me with you.

speaker: (the boy)
text: I know the shop. I do not know the Bell.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Good. Ten shillings apiece when you are back at the book, and not a list of names for the yard to hear.

speaker: margery_pell
text: I have said my line. Butchers' men, and the cook. I am going up to what is mine, which is not this book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Count yours. Leave ours as apiece.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: If the bladder fails I will say so on Saturday. Not before.

speaker: hired_men
text: The baskets are shifting. Mind your feet.

speaker: (the boy)
text: He says aye, and you owe him a cup.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Aye is enough. The cup is mine to owe. He is not in this room.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Then the wages stand at ten shillings apiece, and the carrier's walk is his, not ours.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not going to the Bell. The almanac can say what it says.

speaker: margery_pell
text: And the yard can clap a cook without a second showing. I have a stair to finish.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Saturday for the hand. Tonight for the bladder. I am done.

speaker: hired_men
text: Baskets are clear. Pay the men who carried them when you pay them. I have not asked to be added up.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not add you up. Ten shillings apiece, and a cup I owe my brother. That is the afternoon.
